name: Blue Whale
fact: The LARGEST animal EVER — even bigger than any dinosaur! Its heart is the size of a small car. It sings songs that travel thousands of miles through the ocean. Your daughter the marine biologist might study these one day!

name: Saltwater Crocodile
fact: The largest living reptile! Crocodilians have barely changed in 95 MILLION years — they lived alongside T-Rex and survived the asteroid. Every croc alive today is a real dinosaur-era survivor.

name: Great White Shark
fact: Sharks have been around for 450 million years — longer than dinosaurs, longer than trees! They've survived FIVE mass extinctions. The great white is a top ocean predator, but blue whales are too big to be prey.

name: Humans Today
fact: We arrived so recently that from Earth's perspective, we JUST walked in. But in that tiny time we've mapped the genome, landed on the moon, and figured out what dinosaurs looked like. Pretty wild for a species that's been here 0.002% of the time.

name: African Elephant
fact: The largest land animal alive! Memory like a legend — can remember water sources from droughts decades ago. A living connection to the Ice Age megafauna that walked beside mammoths 20,000 years ago.

name: Dodo (Raphus cucullatus)
fact: The most famous extinction symbol in history - a flightless pigeon that evolved with no natural predators and lost all fear of humans. The last confirmed Dodo was killed in 1681, just 89 years after Europeans first arrived on Mauritius. It became the first species where humans fully documented their own role in an extinction.
know: No complete stuffed dodo survives — only a head and a foot at Oxford. DNA from that head showed the dodo was a giant flightless pigeon; its closest living relative is the Nicobar pigeon of Southeast Asia.

name: Passenger Pigeon (Ectopistes migratorius)
fact: Once the most numerous bird on Earth - flocks of billions darkened the sky for days. In less than 50 years of industrial-scale hunting and forest clearing the species was wiped out entirely. The last individual Martha died at the Cincinnati Zoo on September 1, 1914.

name: Thylacine (Tasmanian Tiger)
fact: A marsupial predator that convergently evolved a dog-like body and striped back despite being more closely related to kangaroos than to any dog. Colonial bounties drove it to extinction. The last known individual died in Hobart Zoo on September 7, 1936 - on the same day it was first granted legal protection.

name: Steller's Sea Cow (Hydrodamalis gigas)
fact: The largest sirenian ever - a gentle giant related to manatees and dugongs that fed on kelp in the freezing North Pacific. Georg Wilhelm Steller discovered it in 1741. Just 27 years later it was hunted to extinction by sailors and fur traders.

name: Giant Moa (Dinornis robustus)
size: Females up to 3.6 m tall, 230 kg
fact: The tallest bird ever known - females towered over modern ostriches. The nine species of moa were New Zealand's dominant herbivores for millions of years. Polynesian settlers arrived around 1280 CE and within 200 years all moa species were extinct, one of the fastest megafaunal collapses in history.

name: Haast's Eagle
fact: The largest eagle known, hunter of New Zealand's giant moa. It died out soon after the moa did.

name: Elephant Bird
fact: Madagascar's giant flightless bird, among the heaviest birds ever. Its eggs held as much as 150 hen's eggs.

name: Koala Lemur (Megaladapis)
fact: A lemur as heavy as a grown man that clung to tree trunks like a koala. It vanished after people reached Madagascar.

name: Aurochs
fact: The wild ancestor of all cattle, painted on cave walls for 30,000 years. The last one died in a Polish forest in 1627.
sites: Jaktorów Forest, Poland — the last one

name: Great Auk
fact: A flightless seabird, the original “penguin”. The last known pair was killed on an Icelandic islet in 1844.

name: Quagga
fact: A zebra with stripes only on its front half. In 1984 it became the first extinct animal to have its DNA studied.

name: Coelacanth
fact: Known only as fossils and thought extinct for 66 million years — until a fisherman caught one off South Africa in 1938. Museum curator Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer recognised it.

name: Horseshoe Crab
fact: Not a crab at all, but a relative of spiders. Its family has looked much the same for over 400 million years, and its blue blood is used to test medicines.

name: Tuatara
fact: It looks like a lizard but is the last survivor of a group that lived alongside the first dinosaurs.

name: Komodo Dragon
fact: The largest living lizard, with a venomous bite. Its giant extinct cousin Megalania once lived in Australia.

name: Platypus
fact: A mammal that lays eggs, has a duck-like bill that senses electricity, and venomous spurs on the males' back legs. When the first one reached Britain in 1799, scientists suspected a hoax.

name: Nautilus
fact: The last of the shelled cephalopods, a living relative of the ammonites. It rises at night and sinks by day by adjusting gas in its shell chambers.

name: Archaeoindris
fact: A lemur the size of a gorilla — the largest primate ever found on Madagascar. It probably lived on the ground, like a giant sloth.

name: Palaeopropithecus (sloth lemur)
fact: A lemur that hung upside down from branches by hooked hands and feet, like a sloth — a primate that evolved into a sloth shape.

name: Malagasy Hippo
fact: Madagascar had its own small hippos — swimming there from Africa, more than once. Some stories collected in the 20th century may describe them.

name: Voay
fact: A horned crocodile, Madagascar's top predator. DNA from its bones (2021) showed its closest relative is the small dwarf crocodile of Africa.

name: Adzebill (Aptornis)
fact: A flightless New Zealand bird with a huge, curved, adze-shaped beak, probably for digging out lizards and big insects.

name: Sylviornis
fact: A giant flightless relative of chickens from New Caledonia, with a bony crest on its beak. It vanished soon after people arrived.
debate: Huge earth mounds on New Caledonia were once thought to be its nests. Most are now thought natural or human-made.

name: Baiji (Yangtze River Dolphin)
fact: A nearly blind river dolphin that hunted by sound in the murky Yangtze. A six-week search of the river in 2006 found none. It is the first dolphin species driven extinct by people.

name: Caribbean Monk Seal
fact: The only seal of the Caribbean, seen by Columbus in 1494. It was hunted for oil, and the last one was seen on a remote reef in 1952.

name: Musk Ox
fact: A living Ice Age giant that walked with the mammoths and survived. When wolves attack, adults form a ring facing outward with the calves inside.

name: Saiga
fact: An Ice Age antelope with a big, droopy nose that warms freezing air in winter and filters dust in summer. In 2015 a bacterial disease killed over 200,000 in three weeks; herds have since recovered.

name: Aye-aye
size: About 40 cm plus a 55 cm tail
fact: A lemur that hunts like a woodpecker: it taps on bark with a long, skeletal middle finger, listens for grubs, gnaws a hole and fishes them out.

name: Okapi
fact: A forest giraffe with zebra-striped legs, unknown to scientists until 1901. Its tongue is long enough to clean its own ears.

name: Narwhal
size: About 4–5 m, plus a tusk up to 3 m
fact: A whale with a spiral tusk — actually a single overgrown tooth, packed with millions of nerve endings. Medieval traders sold the tusks as unicorn horns.

name: Axolotl
fact: A salamander that never grows up: it keeps its frilly gills and stays in the water all its life. It can regrow lost legs, parts of its heart, even parts of its brain.

name: Naked Mole-rat
fact: A wrinkly, nearly hairless rodent that lives in colonies with one breeding queen, like bees. It can live over 30 years, survives 18 minutes without oxygen, and almost never gets cancer.
